messages:
maria: Heads-up — opened PR #1428 to update SDK examples for streaming/pagination/retries across Python/TypeScript/Go. https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1428
alex: Nice. What's the main break users will hit?
maria: The Python streaming example in the current docs uses `for chunk in response:` but the SDK runtime recently changed streaming to return an async generator for async usage and a `stream()` object for sync with an event API. I updated both sync/async examples. Example (async):
```python
# async streaming tokens
async for token in client.chat.stream_async("gpt-xyz", messages):
    print(token.text, end="")
```
and sync: 
```python
# sync streaming (event-based)
for ev in client.chat.stream("gpt-xyz", messages):
    if ev.type == "token":
        print(ev.token, end="")
    elif ev.type == "done":
        break
```
alex: OK. Can you also show a small retry example since a lot of teams rely on built-in retry wrappers?
maria: Yep — added a simple example using the new RetryPolicy helper and explicit backoff settings: 
```python
from redwood import Client, RetryPolicy
client = Client(api_key=..., retries=RetryPolicy(max_attempts=3, backoff="exponential"))
resp = client.generate(model="gpt-xyz", prompt="hi")
```
jason: Go snippet is also out-of-date — current docs use `Stream()` which returned bytes. The runtime now emits typed events (`Token`, `Done`, `Error`). I updated the Go example to show reading a channel of events and handling them. Short sample in the PR.
sophia: I left some TS nits — types and how `stream()` is awaited in the TS SDK changed (now `client.stream(...).subscribe(onEvent)` style). I'll push a small patch to your branch.

maria: Thanks — pushed TS adjustments. New TS example (compact):
```ts
const stream = client.chat.stream("gpt-xyz", { messages });
stream.subscribe({
  onEvent: (e) => {
    if (e.type === 'token') console.log(e.token);
    if (e.type === 'done') console.log('done');
  },
  onError: (err) => console.error(err)
});
```

luke: Small reminder — linkcheck failed previously because the pagination guide link was renamed. docs-bot flagged it. Did you update the internal link?
docs-bot: linkcheck: /docs/guides/pagination moved -> /docs/reference/pagination (auto-suggest).
maria: Fixed the link and added a note in the PR description about the rename. Also updated the pagination example to use the `paginate()` helper and `limit` param for clarity. Example added for Python and TS.

alex: Can we include a short migration note for teams on v0.12 to explain the streaming API change and the recommended pattern for retries? People will hit these during upgrades.
luke: +1 — please also mention the ordering guarantees change for event batching (very small note).
maria: Added a migration snippet at docs/migration.md with a one-paragraph summary and a short code diff. I also added a tiny test snippet under examples/ci that runs the streaming example against a local mock.

sophia: I ran the TS example locally — minor style nit (use `await stream.done()` instead of relying on GC). Pushed that tweak.
alex: Left one small comment about tokenization wording in the Python example (clarify that token fragments may be emitted).
maria: Clarified the wording and added a one-liner explaining partial tokens. Also updated the README code fence formatting to avoid the site Markdown parser bug.

alex: Approving now :thumbsup:
sophia: :eyes: LGTM
jason: Will merge once CI passes.
ci-bot: docs-site build succeeded — deploy scheduled to staging (build #5824).
maria: Thanks everyone — merging now and will backport to the v0.12 branch after the deploy passes.

alex: Quick follow-up: please add a short note in the Python snippet about the tokenizer behavior with streaming outputs (one-liner).
maria: Done. Added the one-liner and a comment in the snippet.
maria: PR merged — thanks all! :tada:
